kubernetes.description: The kubernetes manager ships no default file pattern, so image tags hardcoded inside a chart's templates/ are invisible to Renovate while the same chart's values.yaml pins are bumped. Scoped to templates/ so the vendored upstream CRDs under crds/ -- whose JSON schemas contain `image:` property names, not image references -- stay out of scope.

packageRules.description: The tools images the chart's Jobs and initContainers run in are pinned by digest in values.yaml, so a bump moves tag and digest together and a retagged upstream image changes nothing.

The monitor image is keyed by FDB minor version in the operator initContainers map -- each entry copies libfdb_c_<key>.so, so the tag must stay on that minor. Renovate sees three occurrences of one repository and bumps them all to latest, which breaks the init container. Bump these by hand alongside fdb.version.

The management plane's own charts are each pinned twice -- as the xp-mp chart's dependency, and as the helm Release the installation composition installs onto the management cluster -- and scripts/check-versions.sh holds the two equal. Renovate sees the dependency and not the Composition, so a bump it made alone would fail that check rather than land. Both copies move by hand, in one change. Crossplane carries a second reason: the boot plane and the management plane must agree across the handover, where a composite created by one is adopted by the other, and a control-plane version also has to be reconciled against the provider and function packages it runs, which Renovate bumps separately.

The Keycloak Operator is expected to run the same version as the Keycloak it manages. The instance's image is pinned in the queenswood chart's values.yaml and the operator's in its vendored subchart at charts/keycloak-operator/templates/operator.yaml, so they still move together. That PR only rewrites the operator's image tag: the subchart is a vendored copy of upstream's kustomize output, so its ClusterRoles and the CRDs under crds/ must be re-vendored from the matching release tag in the same change, and both Chart.yaml appVersions updated.

Every direct npm dependency is declared `^X.Y.Z`, and `bump` raises that floor with each update rather than moving the lockfile alone, so a package two members declare reads as one version in `poly libs`. CI runs `yarn dedupe --check`, and an update that raises a shared transitive dependency leaves the old copy resolved beside the new unless the lockfile is deduplicated after it.
